reasons: Lake identity verifies United States v. Smith, Fifth Circuit, decided 2024-08-09, docket 23-60321.
Lake citations identify the official/display citation as 110 F.4th 817, matching the page's reporter citation and year/court fields.
The opinion expressly applies Carpenter to Google Location History and says the third-party doctrine does not apply.
That makes a Third-Party Doctrine & CSLI cross-reference supportable as related rather than primary.

defect.evidence_quote: they never include a specific user to be identified, only a temporal and geographic location where any given user may turn up post-search.
defect.problem: The holding is materially supported, but the phrase 'identify everyone in an area' is too broad because the opinion describes searches and returns involving Google accounts/devices with Location History enabled, not literally every person in the area.
defect.proposed_fix: Change to: 'which identify Google users/devices with Location History enabled in or near a defined area rather than a particularized suspect.'

reasons: The search-threshold proposition is supported: the court held law enforcement conducted a search when it sought Location History data from Google.

The general-warrant and good-faith propositions are directly supported by the conclusion: geofence warrants are modern-day general warrants, unconstitutional, but suppression was unwarranted under good faith.
residual_risks: A separate quote-fidelity/pincite row was not inventoried, though the page contains a pinned conclusion quote.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use 'Google users/devices with Location History enabled' instead of 'everyone in an area.'

reasons: The opinion is a Fifth Circuit geofence-warrant decision holding geofence acquisition is a search and geofence warrants are categorically unconstitutional general warrants.
The court says it parts ways with the Fourth Circuit, supporting the 'circuit anchor' role for geofence warrants.
Treatment/currency is outside Lens A; the asserted treatment fields match the disclosed lake treatment judgment fields and content frontmatter.
residual_risks: No independent Lens A review of Chatrie or currency was performed.

reasons: Treatment/currency is outside Lens A; the asserted point override matches the disclosed lake point_overrides entry for search.warrant.geofence-general-warrant.
residual_risks: No independent Lens A review of the Chatrie limitation was performed.

reasons: The authority-weight label is consistent with the disclosed identity fields: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit, circuit 5th.
Treatment/currency is outside Lens A, and no support or quote-fidelity defect appears in this label.
